newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Gov files plan to deregulate generation.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Gov files plan to deregulate generation.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld filed legislation on Monday seeking to have electric generation services deregulated and subject to open market competition.
Weld noted the utilities' major concern of recovering so-called stranded costs -- the cost of investments and power purchase agreements which might not be fully recoverable in the competitive market.

Under his measure, utilities will be able to pass those costs onto consumers after proving they have tried to recover the costs through the sale of generation plants and buy-outs of power purchase contracts.

"This law will allow consumers to choose which company they want generating their juice," Weld told reporters at a statehouse news conference. "Opening up the electric utilitiy industry to competition will drive down rates and reduce the burden that utility costs place on everyone's pocketbook."
He estimated the program would cut consumers' electric rates by at least 10 percent.

The measure also calls for the Department of Environmental Protection to develop generation performance standards to regulate the pollution produced as a result of providing power to Massachusetts customers.

The law would also protect municipalities that host power plants. For those municipalities facing a decrease in property tax revenue due to electric restructuring, the bill establsihes a formula for a five-year transition from current assessments on power plants to real market valuation.
Massachusetts consumers spend $4.5 billion annually on electricty, the governor said.
